# Windows desktop build (Electron)

The desktop app is the same Vite bundle the web and phone builds use, wrapped in
a small Electron shell. It exists so the library keeps working on a laptop with
no connection - the same situation the phone app is in while the Supabase
project is over quota.

## Build

```bash
npm install                     # once; installs electron + electron-builder
npm run desktop:run             # build + open the app (dev window, DevTools menu)
npm run desktop:package         # build + installer + portable exe
```

Output lands in `releases/desktop/`:

| File | Size | Use |
|------|------|-----|
| `GoStudy-1.3.4-setup.exe` | ~169 MB | Installer, per-user, desktop + Start-menu shortcuts |
| `GoStudy-1.3.4-portable.exe` | ~137 MB | Single exe, no install (unpacks to temp) |
| `win-unpacked/` | - | Unpacked app; used by the smoke tests |

The exe is **not code-signed**, so Windows SmartScreen shows "unknown
publisher" on first launch. Personal use: choose *More info -> Run anyway*. A
certificate is only needed to remove that prompt.

## What is inside

`electron/catalog/` is generated by `npm run desktop:catalog`
(`scripts/desktop/prepare-catalog.mjs`) from the published R2 catalogue:

- `papers.json` (395 rows), `books.json` (415 rows), `feed.json` (5 posts)
- `assets/feed/*.png` - the five Actus flyers, so Actus renders offline on a
  fresh install

That folder is git-ignored; it is rebuilt from `scripts/r2/output/catalog` on
every package run. PDFs are **not** bundled - the shell caches them on first
open instead.

## How the shell works

`electron/main.cjs` does four things:

1. **Serves `dist/` on `http://127.0.0.1:47821`.** A real http origin keeps
   `BrowserRouter`, the service worker and the R2 CORS rules identical to the
   web build. If the port is busy it walks up to `47831`.
2. **Serves the catalogue at `/catalog/*.json`,** rewriting every
   `https://pub-...r2.dev` URL to `/r2/...`. Keys, ordering and all other fields
   are untouched, so the renderer behaves exactly as it does against R2.
3. **Caches R2 objects at `/r2/<key>`** under
   `%APPDATA%/GoStudy/cache/r2/<key>`. First request downloads and stores; later
   requests (including offline ones) are served from disk. The cache prunes
   itself to 6 GB (limit 8 GB) at startup.
4. **Refreshes the catalogue in the background** every 6 hours when online, into
   `%APPDATA%/GoStudy/catalog/`. A refreshed copy wins over the bundled one; a
   failed or invalid download never replaces it.

The renderer keeps its normal flow: Supabase first, then `catalog/*.json` (this
is why `VITE_CATALOG_URL=/catalog` lives in `.env.desktop`).

## Offline behaviour

| Feature | Fresh install, offline | After opening once online |
|---|---|---|
| Library lists, filters, counts | Works (bundled catalogue) | Works |
| Actus posts + flyers | Works (bundled) | Works |
| Paper/book PDF | "not opened on this computer yet" | Works (disk cache) |
| Previews/thumbnails | Placeholder | Works (disk cache) |
| Grades, settings, downloads list | Works (local IndexedDB) | Works |

## Smoke tests

`main.cjs` accepts test flags; reports are written to
`<userData>/smoke-report.json` because the packaged exe is a GUI binary:

```bash
# development tree
npx electron . --smoke --screenshot shot.png
npx electron . --smoke --offline

# packaged app, isolated profile, Actus page
releases/desktop/win-unpacked/GoStudy.exe \
  --user-data-dir=%TEMP%\gostudy-test --smoke --offline \
  --route /courses --screenshot %TEMP%\feed.png
```

The report lists catalogue counts (395/415/5), the status of a PDF request
(`200` served, `503` = not cached while offline) and the first 300 characters of
the rendered page.

Verified on the packaged build:

| Run | papers | books | feed | PDF |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| fresh profile, offline | 395 | 415 | 5 | 503 (expected) |
| same profile, online | 395 | 415 | 5 | 200 |
| same profile, offline again | 395 | 415 | 5 | 200 (from cache) |
| portable exe, offline | 395 | 415 | 5 | 503 (expected) |

## Updating the app

`electron-builder.yml` sets `extraMetadata.version: 1.3.4`; `package.json`
stays at `0.0.0` because Android/iOS carry their own version fields. Bump the
`extraMetadata.version` for a new desktop release, then rerun
`npm run desktop:package`.

The catalogue updates itself, so a new paper or book only needs a reinstall if
the change has to work offline out of the box; otherwise it appears as soon as
the machine is online.
